claims.text: The initial cast alloy is equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr exhibits 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr exhibits a high-temperature yield strength of 163–530 MPa.
Untreated equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has inadequate oxygen resistance.
Untreated equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr undergoes rapid oxidation during high-temperature air exposure.
Untreated equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr suffers pesting during high-temperature air exposure.
Pack cementation aluminizing can deposit an Al-rich surface layer on equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr.
Aluminizing at 900–950 °C for 1–2 hours will form a graded Al-rich diffusion layer.
The graded Al-rich layer will preferentially oxidize to form a continuous alumina scale.
The alumina scale produced by the treatment will adhere to the substrate.
The continuous alumina scale will limit oxygen ingress into the alloy.
Optimization of the aluminizing heat treatment will minimize Al diffusion into the bulk alloy.
Minimizing bulk diffusion will preserve the alloy's near-surface microstructure.
Preserving the near-surface microstructure will preserve the alloy's mechanical properties.
Aluminizing will reduce oxidation rates relative to untreated equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr during air exposure at 800–1000 °C for up to 5 hours.
Aluminizing will reduce pesting relative to untreated equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr during air exposure at 800–1000 °C for up to 5 hours.
The treated alloy will retain room-temperature tensile ductility comparable to that of the untreated alloy.
The treated alloy will retain high-temperature yield strength comparable to that of the untreated alloy at strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
